name: ShadowCode v2.4.1
body:
# ShadowCode 2.4.1

This patch addresses a layout defect found while qualifying the public 2.4.0
Windows installer: at 175% zoom in a short window, the composer could extend
past the conversation area and cover the terminal dock’s Hide control.

## Short windows and larger text

- Keep the dock and header controls separate from the conversation. In short
  docked layouts, the conversation and composer scroll within their own area.
- Keep composer actions and menus reachable, including slash commands, mentions,
  permissions and model selection, without discarding an unsent draft.
- Keep the Latest activity control reachable when returning to recent output.
- Provide a scrolling fallback for engines without size container queries.
- Preserve the open editor draft and existing terminal session when hiding,
  restoring or moving the terminal.
- Display the folder name correctly for Windows paths and reserve two complete
  terminal rows, including their padding and borders. Long notices, errors,
  tabs and restart controls remain accessible in a separate scrollable area.

## Startup and project navigation

- Prevent delayed post-onboarding startup from restoring an older conversation
  after the user has created or selected a newer one.
- Keep late workspace, configuration, Git and trust results from overwriting a
  newer navigation choice. Project opening and conversation activation share
  the same ordered queue.
- Preserve normal saved-session restoration and existing appearance callbacks.

The correction covers layout, terminal path labels, startup navigation and
regression coverage. It does not change model backends, command permissions,
signing keys or sandbox policy. The source
release trust ceiling is extended to 2.4.1 using the existing Linux signing key.
AppStream metadata is checked against application versions before packaging.

The 2.4.0 release remains immutable. Its failed Windows interface qualification,
successful installer/endurance checks and incomplete real-model attempt remain
separately recorded in [platform qualification](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/blob/main/docs/PLATFORM_QUALIFICATION.md).
Browser regression coverage is distinct from the exact public-installer checks;
consult that record for version-specific native qualification status, results
and limitations.

## Validation

The corrected patch passed 928 interface unit tests and all 170 Chromium browser
tests. Focused WebKit coverage passed 32 existing workspace checks and the four
new terminal-layout checks; the latter use the browser's supported Option-Tab
navigation. After the startup correction, eight focused WebKit first-run and
conversation-navigation cases passed as well. Type checking, the production
build and bundle checks passed.

The terminal regressions fail against the earlier candidate in both Chromium
and WebKit. They cover long Windows paths, long folder names, errors, multiple
tabs, exit/restart controls, complete visible rows and accessible notices. The
original 12 composer regressions also failed against the 2.4.0 stylesheet.
Linux release-authentication tests passed 115 checks, and the updated Debian
packaging/metadata suites passed 19, including an early AppStream version check.

Controlled startup tests delay refresh, session lookup and project opening,
then verify that newer choices remain selected in the UI and active at the
backend API boundary. The app-level regression fails against the previous
candidate. See the [source validation record](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/blob/main/docs/qa/onboarding-navigation-2.4.1/verification.json). Additional tests preserve normal startup, trust prompts and existing
theme/text-size callbacks. These tests use a simulated backend.

A separate review-before-commit test timing race was corrected without changing
the application's commit guard. Browser checks use a simulated backend; exact
native installer qualification is recorded separately in the platform record.

---

# ShadowCode 2.4.0

ShadowCode 2.4 introduces a simpler first run, a more accessible coding workspace
for Apple Silicon Macs, revision-aware review, and bounded local-runtime
reliability improvements. It builds on the existing Metal runtime and preserves
project trust, approvals, editor drafts and engine-owned terminal sessions.

## Start work from the conversation

- **One first-run screen.** Open a project and arrive in the conversation with
  ask-first approvals. Model setup stays on the empty conversation instead of
  a second blocking wizard. Starter cards fill the composer without sending
  a task or changing permissions.
- **Connect where you choose a model.** Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity
  and Grok use their vendor sign-in flows; Antigravity can Install & connect.
  Enter OpenRouter, xAI or OpenAI keys inline, or explicitly choose a local
  download. New keys use the macOS Keychain or Linux desktop keyring when
  available. Settings › Accounts remains the place to manage connections.
- **Clear conversation state.** Sidebar conversations show Working, Done or
  Needs approval. Project-specific New task actions join the activation queue,
  so delayed creation cannot override a later selection. Changes leads into
  the existing commit and Open pull request workflow.

## Files, conversation and terminal together

- **Direct workspace controls.** Files, Terminal and Preview are available in
  the toolbar. Resize the side pane with a pointer or keyboard; its preferred
  width is remembered and clamped to leave room for the conversation.
- **Optional terminal dock.** Keep Files and the conversation visible above a
  terminal. Commands focus the existing dock without replacing dirty Files or
  creating a second shell. Hiding the dock restores workspace focus while the
  shell keeps running. A delayed terminal mount respects a newer editor or
  composer focus choice; palette commands transfer focus after dialog cleanup.
  Toolbar active and pressed states reflect the visible surfaces.
- **Layout follows text size.** Split layouts preserve at least 380 layout
  pixels for the conversation and use overlays at compact widths. Sidebar,
  drawer and toolbar states use effective width under CSS fallback zoom;
  native webview zoom retains its independent scaling path. Dock controls and
  the rendered terminal screen remain separate from the compact drawer.
- **Project context and explicit checks.** Folder, branch, project checks and
  latest-task review are accessible from the workspace. Run a project check
  before the first model turn or from completed-task evidence, using the normal
  trust and approval flow. The composer draft is retained; task completion is
  not treated as verification.
- **Mac keyboard and reduced motion.** Command-Shift-M opens the model picker;
  Control-backtick reaches Terminal. Command-M and Command-backtick remain
  available to native window behavior. Option-arrow editing and IME composition
  stay with text input. The terminal cursor follows Reduce Motion changes
  without restarting its shell. Drawer closing restores its trigger when
  appropriate and respects a later focus choice.

## Review freshness and recovery

Keep markers identify the file revision actually shown. A content change
invalidates file and hunk markers; legacy path-only marks do not attest to a
current revision. Task-owned request generations reject stale list/detail
responses, including navigation and undo races. Undo All revalidates whole-file
Keep marks before deciding what to undo. Rejected, busy and no-op undo paths
replace an interrupted detail read without overwriting a later valid selection.
Keep remains a review marker, not a disk write or Git staging operation.

## Apple Silicon and local-runtime reliability

- **Native packaging and Metal resources.** Packaging prefers arm64 on Apple
  Silicon even from a Rosetta shell. The bundled llama.cpp Metal runtime requires
  its compiled `default.metallib`, and sets the shader-resource path at runtime.
  Doctor reports processor/Rosetta identity and shader availability. Metal is
  existing macOS support, not a newly introduced backend; Linux packages support
  Vulkan/CPU and the Windows package uses CPU execution.
- **Shared-memory accounting.** Correct speculative-page accounting and recheck
  fresh estimated headroom before allocation on positively identified Apple
  Metal hardware, with a 2 GiB reserve. CPU retries use the same shared-memory
  check after the previous child exits. Unknown or inconsistent telemetry is
  not a hard refusal; estimates neither reserve memory nor guarantee allocation.
- **Bounded cache policy.** Disable the audited pinned runtime's extra host
  prompt cache with revision-gated arguments. The active KV cache is unchanged.
  This bounds one allocation source; it is not a speed improvement claim and
  can increase recomputation across requests.
- **Cancellation that stays truthful.** Cancel pending model preparation from
  Local models. Readiness waits can be interrupted and their child cleaned up.
  If cancellation is refused, the UI continues tracking the original load until
  it settles instead of incorrectly reporting an unloaded model.
- **Mac developer tools and readable commands.** Allow required system-temp
  metadata access for Apple developer tools when using an external temp folder,
  while retaining restrictions on unrelated temp contents and writes. Darwin
  temp-folder identifiers are no longer mistaken for high-entropy secrets on
  command cards.

## Validation and scope

The frozen implementation passed:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI unit tests | 906 passed in 157 files |
| Full Chromium suite | 154 passed |
| Focused WebKit suite | 35 passed |
| Native core unit tests | 677 passed; 8 ignored |
| Native review/API integration | 9 passed |
| Native local-engine integration | 33 passed; 3 ignored |
| TypeScript, rustfmt, workspace Clippy and production test-fixture isolation | Passed |

Browser automation uses deterministic service fixtures. Geometry checks include
800/1160/1440-pixel viewports at 100/125/175% CSS zoom with the sidebar enabled
and disabled; focus tests hold terminal listing pending while another editing
surface takes focus. These results include the final palette focus correction.

A bounded Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0 service check on an Apple Silicon Mac completed load,
a short response, same-model reuse, unload, reload, and cleanup after an injected
failure. This establishes that lifecycle for the tested small model. It is not
a performance benchmark, coding-quality assessment, large-model qualification,
or proof of observed Metal layer offload. Device discovery and requested GPU
placement remain distinct from measured execution. No percentage speed claim
is made.

Native VoiceOver, non-US physical keyboards, broad hardware coverage and
sustained memory-pressure behavior are outside these results. The verified
ARM64 development app is ad-hoc signed; development-build and browser results do
not by themselves qualify a distribution installer or establish notarization.
Vendor CLIs still require their own installation/sign-in unless an explicit
Install & connect path is offered; there is no vendor-password form.

See the [implementation and qualification record](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/blob/main/docs/MAC_FLAGSHIP_UPGRADE.md),
[local-model documentation](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/blob/main/docs/LOCAL_MODELS.md),
and [user guide](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/blob/main/docs/USER_GUIDE.md).
Version-specific assets and installation instructions belong to their verified
[GitHub release](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/releases);
source version numbers alone do not establish published download availability.

# ShadowCode 2.3.3

Linux x64 and ARM64 packages are published and authenticated with the existing release signing key. Windows, macOS and Flatpak packages are also published. Version 2.3.2 was not published because its signing policy did not authorize that version; its tag remains unchanged. Version 2.3.3 extends the existing key's trust interval and adds a release preflight for policy mismatches.

This release fixes an Omarchy AppImage desktop-startup failure, a model-picker focus race, unsolicited interactive Grok login during provider discovery, and Mac keyboard hints. On the Omarchy laptop, the authenticated public 2.3.3 AppImage passed installation, first-window and 12 focused Wayland interface checks. Its installed engine separately passed 100 sequential and 80 concurrent scripted-provider tasks, five cancellations and persistence after restart. These checks do not establish real-model inference, GPU endurance or cloud-provider compatibility. See the [physical-machine qualification](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/blob/main/docs/PLATFORM_QUALIFICATION.md) for details and limitations. On the Windows 11 laptop, the public 2.3.3 installer passed installation, native editor and settings checks, and scripted-provider engine endurance; a real Gemma 4 E4B CPU coding task also passed with the original five tests preserved and independently rechecked. This is one task, not broad model-quality qualification. On the Intel iMac, the public package passed installation, native-window startup and scripted-provider engine endurance. Screen capture was unavailable, so physical iMac visual editing and keyboard interaction were not verified; real-model inference was not tested there.

# ShadowCode 2.3.2 — unpublished candidate

The 2.3.2 candidate supplied the fixes above; its evidence remains historical and does not qualify the 2.3.3 packages.

The new platform endurance probe exercises the installed native engine against
a loopback scripted provider. It measures 100 sequential tasks, 80 concurrent
tasks, five cancellations, process resource growth, and persisted state after
stopping/reopening. It does not certify desktop rendering, paid-provider
accounts, real-model quality, GPU inference, or inference-server memory.
Windows persistence is tested after forced process termination; graceful
Windows shutdown is not claimed by that probe.

# ShadowCode 2.3.1

Write-subagent guidance now names its Git-history prerequisite and directs
plain-folder tasks to direct editing or read-only agents. A prerequisite check
runs before worktree preparation, with regression coverage for plain folders,
unborn repositories and committed repositories.

The public Windows installer passed installation, clean-PATH startup, native
editor/settings checks and a bounded Gemma 4 E4B coding task on a Windows 11
x64 laptop. The agent ran tests inside AppContainer; all five original tests
were preserved and passed independently. Windows local inference is CPU-only;
Windows 10, ARM, GPU and real cloud-provider accounts remain unqualified on
that hardware. The installer is not code-signed.

Version 2.3.1 is published for Windows, Linux and macOS. It does not change
Windows AppContainer permissions: external Git commands that open the null device can
still fail inside the sandbox. See the [Windows port notes](WINDOWS_PORT.md)
and [qualification record](WINDOWS_LAPTOP_QUALIFICATION.md). The published
2.3.0 notes follow below.

# ShadowCode 2.3.0

ShadowCode 2.3.0 runs on Windows. The 2.2.0 notes follow below.

## New

- **ShadowCode for Windows.** `ShadowCode_2.3.0_x64-setup.exe` for 64-bit
  Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) and 11 installs for your user, without
  administrator rights. Local models run on llama.cpp (CPU), terminals open
  PowerShell, and subscription tools such as Codex and Claude Code run
  through their Windows command-line programs. Install or update with one PowerShell command (see
  the [README](../README.md#windows)); a copy downloaded in a browser shows
  **Windows protected your PC** the first time: choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**.
- **A sandbox for agent commands on Windows.** Commands run in a contained
  shell that can change only the project, sees Windows, Program Files and
  your toolchains read-only, cannot see the rest of your home folder, and
  has no network unless you turn it on. Commands keep their usual `sh`
  syntax. **Only allowed hosts** is not available on Windows.

## Fixed

- Two parts of ShadowCode saving settings at the same moment no longer fail
  on Windows with "Access is denied", and busy databases no longer time out
  with "database is locked".

- The Windows installer includes the Microsoft runtime DLLs needed to start
  the app and local models on a machine without development tools.
- Sandboxed commands now wait for the child process and return its actual
  output and exit status instead of sometimes reporting empty success.
- Windows redo accepts both Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z, and worktree setup uses
  the platform shell.
- Selecting a local GGUF model from a fresh CLI process works without first
  opening the model picker.

## Known limits

- The Windows version is new and has been tested on GitHub's Windows
  machines and one Windows 11 laptop, not yet on a wide range of PCs.
  Both the optimized Windows preview and release-workflow installer
  completed a small Python repair task with Gemma 4 E4B on CPU, with the
  original tests preserved and independently passing. This is not broad
  model-quality qualification; see the
  [qualification record](WINDOWS_LAPTOP_QUALIFICATION.md).
  Subscription tools were tested
  there with stand-in programs, not yet with each vendor's own Windows CLI.
  Local models use the CPU only on Windows for now.

## Download

Linux x86_64: `ShadowCode_2.3.0_amd64.AppImage`, `ShadowCode_2.3.0_amd64.deb`
and `ShadowCode_2.3.0_appimage-runtime-sources.tar.gz`, with `SHA256SUMS`,
`RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`, `RELEASE-AUTH` and `RELEASE-AUTH.sig`. For ARM64 the
packages end in `_aarch64` (AppImage) or `_arm64` (`.deb`), with signature
files ending in `-aarch64`. Install the AppImage with the authenticated
installer described in the [README](../README.md#install); the signature is
checked before anything runs. The Flatpak bundles, the macOS disk images and
the Windows installer are attached shortly after publication, with their
SHA-256 checksums in `ShadowCode_2.3.0_flatpak.sha256`,
`ShadowCode_2.3.0_macos.sha256` and `ShadowCode_2.3.0_windows.sha256`; the
complete source of the busybox-w32 shell bundled for Windows is
`ShadowCode_2.3.0_busybox-w32-source.tar.gz`.

# ShadowCode 2.2.0

ShadowCode 2.2.0 runs on Macs, both Apple silicon and Intel, and its Linux
Flatpak is now a download on every release. It also connects to your own
model servers and adds find in conversation, a smarter command palette and
text size. The 2.1.0 notes follow below.

## New

- **ShadowCode for macOS.** `ShadowCode_2.2.0_aarch64.dmg` for Apple silicon
  and `ShadowCode_2.2.0_x64.dmg` for Intel Macs (macOS 12 or later). Local
  models run on llama.cpp with Metal; agent shell commands run in the macOS
  sandbox, with your home folder and other drives hidden; API keys can be
  kept in the Keychain. Install or update with one command, or open the
  `.dmg` (see the [README](../README.md#macos); a copy downloaded in a
  browser needs **Open Anyway** in Privacy & Security the first time).
- **The Flatpak on every release.** `ShadowCode_2.2.0_x86_64.flatpak` and
  `ShadowCode_2.2.0_aarch64.flatpak`, with the Vulkan GPU runtime, built,
  installed and started from the release before they are attached.
- **Your own model servers.** **Settings › Accounts › Your own endpoints**
  connects Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM servers, xAI, OpenAI or any
  OpenAI-compatible API; the models you pick run with ShadowCode's own agent.
- **Settings › Agent.** Steps, budgets, time limits, retries, history
  shortening, checkpoints and more, each with its range, default and Reset.
- **Find in conversation** (`Ctrl+F`), search that also matches answers, a
  command palette that matches letters in order and lists conversations and
  projects, **text size** (`Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-`, `Ctrl+0`), message times, and
  **Show all** and **Copy** for long tool output.

## Fixed

- **Approval cards show the folder a command runs in.** Long paths such as
  `/Volumes/Disk2/projects/app` could be hidden as if they were secrets.
- **Low memory is named before a model loads.** A local model that needs
  more memory than is free right now says so, instead of running very slowly.
- The theme follows the desktop by default, and screen readers hear
  milestones rather than every streamed update.

## Download

Linux x86_64: `ShadowCode_2.2.0_amd64.AppImage`, `ShadowCode_2.2.0_amd64.deb`
and `ShadowCode_2.2.0_appimage-runtime-sources.tar.gz`, with `SHA256SUMS`,
`RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`, `RELEASE-AUTH` and `RELEASE-AUTH.sig`. For ARM64 the
packages end in `_aarch64` (AppImage) or `_arm64` (`.deb`), with signature
files ending in `-aarch64`. Install the AppImage with the authenticated
installer described in the [README](../README.md#install); the signature is
checked before anything runs. The Flatpak bundles and the macOS disk images
are attached shortly after publication, with their SHA-256 checksums in
`ShadowCode_2.2.0_flatpak.sha256` and `ShadowCode_2.2.0_macos.sha256`.

# ShadowCode 2.1.0

ShadowCode 2.1.0 runs on 64-bit ARM computers, installs and updates from a
signed APT repository, and its installer now checks that the new version
starts before it keeps it. The 2.0.0 notes follow below.

## New

- **64-bit ARM.** The AppImage, the Debian package and the Flatpak are built
  and tested on ARM64 (aarch64) as well as x86_64, and each is signed for its
  own architecture. Download the files ending in `_aarch64` or `_arm64`.
- **Updates through APT.** Add the signed ShadowCode repository once and
  `apt upgrade` keeps ShadowCode current, on both architectures. The README's
  Debian section shows how, including how to check the repository's key.
- **An installer that checks before it commits.** The AppImage installer
  saves a copy of your database, starts the new version and waits for its
  window. If it hangs, crashes or reports the wrong version, everything is put
  back as it was, database included.
- **Model history in the picker.** Each model shows how long tasks took in
  this project, what they cost when the provider reported it, and how often
  their checks passed. **Compare history** shows them side by side, and an
  optional suggestion points to the cheapest model that passed here before.
  ShadowCode never switches models on its own.

## Fixed

- **The window remembers its size again**, including on Wayland desktops
  such as KDE Plasma, without growing from launch to launch.
- **Website allow-list in the Flatpak.** Agent shell commands in the Flatpak
  can now be limited to the websites you allow; if that can't be set up, the
  command is refused rather than run unrestricted.

## Download

For x86_64: `ShadowCode_2.1.0_amd64.AppImage`, `ShadowCode_2.1.0_amd64.deb`
and `ShadowCode_2.1.0_appimage-runtime-sources.tar.gz`, with `SHA256SUMS`,
`RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`, `RELEASE-AUTH` and `RELEASE-AUTH.sig`. For ARM64 the
packages end in `_aarch64` (AppImage) or `_arm64` (`.deb`), with signature
files ending in `-aarch64`. Install the AppImage with the authenticated
installer described in the [README](../README.md#install); the signature is
checked before anything runs.

# ShadowCode 2.0.0

Version 2.0.0 adds a source-built Flatpak, closes three reproduced remote-access defects, and updates the affected development dependency. See [Flatpak](FLATPAK.md) for installation, host-tool permissions, and package-specific limits. The source is published in this repository; binary release publication and Flathub submission remain pending. About ShadowCode shows the version, Apache license, publisher, official website, repository, and contributors. The [trademark and branding policy](../TRADEMARKS.md) covers the official identity and permits forks and accurate community attribution. Previous release notes follow.

# ShadowCode 1.0.1

ShadowCode 1.0.1 fixes the size of the window: it no longer grows each time
it opens on Wayland, and it fits small screens. The 1.0.0 notes follow below.

## Fixed

- **The window no longer grows each time it opens.** On Wayland desktops
  such as KDE Plasma, the window opened a little bigger every time (about 50
  pixels wider and 100 taller) until it no longer fit on the screen.
  ShadowCode no longer remembers the window's size on any desktop, so it
  opens at its default size, fitted to the screen. It still reopens
  maximized or full screen if you left it that way, and on X11 at the same
  place. If your window already grew, it opens at its normal size again.
- **The window fits small screens.** On a 1366x768 screen the window used to
  be taller than the screen, so the composer and the status bar were hidden
  under the panel. The window now opens at a size that fits the screen, with
  room for the title bar and the panel. With more than one screen it fits
  the screen it reopens on (X11), or every screen (Wayland, where the
  desktop chooses). Larger screens still get the full size, the window opens
  maximized only when no screen is big enough for it, and a window you left
  maximized opens maximized.

## Download

`ShadowCode_1.0.1_amd64.AppImage`, `ShadowCode_1.0.1_amd64.deb` and
`ShadowCode_1.0.1_appimage-runtime-sources.tar.gz`, with `SHA256SUMS`,
`RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`, `RELEASE-AUTH` and `RELEASE-AUTH.sig`. Install the
AppImage with the authenticated installer described in the
[README](../README.md#install); the signature is checked before anything
runs.

## Published 1.0.0

[ShadowCode 1.0.0](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/releases/tag/v1.0.0)
made ShadowCode easy to start and ready for real work. New users get free
models first, plain explanations when something fails and a glossary of the
words the app uses. Everyone gets approvals that explain themselves, secret
checks before anything leaves the computer, one rulebook for every agent,
second opinions from another model, spending limits, and tools for big
projects.

### Easy to start

- **Free models first.** Until you connect a subscription, the model picker
  lists the free models on this computer first. Your code stays on your
  machine.
- **Plain words when something fails.** If a task fails because a key was
  refused, credits ran out, the conversation got too long, the model doesn't
  exist, the provider is busy, the local model isn't running or you're
  offline, ShadowCode says so simply and offers the next step, such as
  **Try again** or **Continue on another model…**.
- **Words you'll see.** Press `?` for Help: it explains worktree,
  checkpoint, rewind, context, tokens and more.
- **Approvals you can read.** Every approval card says what the action does
  in one sentence, how much it can affect, and whether Rewind can undo it,
  even for long shell commands and for Codex, Claude Code and the other
  subscriptions.

### Safe by default

- **No secrets by accident.** Commits, pushes and pull requests from
  ShadowCode are checked for keys, passwords and `.env` files first; you
  choose to remove the file, ignore it, or go ahead.
- **Careful with new packages.** When the agent wants to install a package,
  ShadowCode checks that it exists, how new it is, and whether its name is a
  near-copy of a popular one.
- **Your keys in the keyring.** API keys can be moved into the system
  keyring (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, KeePassXC) with one click.
- **Heads-ups.** If a task skipped or deleted tests, changed CI or switched
  off a check, the conversation says so. **Only change these** keeps a task
  to the files you name.
- **Always allow here** for the exact test and build commands you run all
  day, per project, and easy to take back.

### Ready for real work

- **One rulebook for every agent.** Write your rules and skills once; they
  reach ShadowCode's own agent and every subscription CLI.
- **Second opinions.** Have another model review your staged changes or a
  task before you commit, with each finding on the line it's about.
- **Roles.** Use one model to plan, another to implement and a third to
  review.
- **Spending limits.** Paid models ask before spending more than $1 on a task
  or $10 in a day (you can change both), and show a price before you send.
- **Recovers on its own.** Busy providers are retried with a visible count;
  after a plan limit, a task can resume when the plan resets; a stuck task
  pauses and asks you.
- **Big projects.** The code index is kept between runs, covers up to 250,000
  files and can focus on one folder of a monorepo.
- **Review by risk.** Changed files are grouped with config and dependencies
  first, and **Explain this change** describes a file's change in plain
  words.
- **Parallel tasks that just work.** A task in its own worktree can start
  from any branch, runs your setup commands, gets your `.env` and its own
  port.

### Reliable

- **Your data is safe.** Back up, restore, repair or start over from
  Settings › Your data. Upgrades from every release since 0.28 are tested.
- A model that runs out of graphics memory offers a smaller context; a task
  that fails early ends with its reason; subscription usage is kept when a
  turn fails; Rewind keeps files you saved during a subscription turn.
- A stable, documented API for version 1.

### Download

`ShadowCode_1.0.0_amd64.AppImage`, `ShadowCode_1.0.0_amd64.deb` and
`ShadowCode_1.0.0_appimage-runtime-sources.tar.gz`, with `SHA256SUMS`,
`RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`, `RELEASE-AUTH` and `RELEASE-AUTH.sig`. Install the
AppImage with the authenticated installer described in the
[README](../README.md#install); the signature is checked before anything
runs.

## Published 0.34.2

[ShadowCode 0.34.2](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/releases/tag/v0.34.2)
made ShadowCode ready for everyone: you can start with no account at all,
the app tells you when an update is out, and a full quality pass fixed dozens
of bugs across the engine, the window, the vendors and security.

### Start with nothing

- **No account needed.** Open a project and ShadowCode offers a free model
  that runs on your own computer, picked for your memory and graphics card,
  with its size and download time. You can also add an OpenRouter key or
  sign in to a subscription.
- **Five free models** to choose from in Settings › Local models, from a
  2 GB model for small laptops to a 19 GB one for big GPUs. Each download is
  checked against a pinned fingerprint, can be paused and resumed, and never
  starts on its own.

### Easier every day

- **A calmer composer.** Effort, Compare and Worktree now live under
  **More**, so the message area stays clear.
- **Clearer when something goes wrong.** Errors read as plain sentences with
  a **Try again** button, and the status bar says "Not connected" when the
  engine is down.
- **Keyboard friendly.** Escape closes every dialog, and the Tasks panel can
  be driven entirely from the keyboard.
- **Update notice.** ShadowCode checks for a new release at most once a day,
  sends nothing about you, and tells you how to update your kind of install.
  **Settings › About** shows the version and license.

### Works with today's tools

Checked live against the current Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok and
Antigravity releases. Claude Code now shows its real models and plan usage,
effort settings work for Claude Code, Codex and Grok, and OpenRouter shows
your account balance.

### Safer and more reliable

- Rewind and Undo can no longer delete files that existed before a task.
- Slow local models on a CPU are no longer cut off mid-answer, and a long
  prompt can take up to 15 minutes to start without being cancelled.
- A security audit closed ways secret files could be read, tightened "Allow
  for this task", blocked DNS rebinding against remote access, and found no
  known vulnerabilities in dependencies.
- The Debian package passes lintian cleanly and is ready for distributions,
  with a man page and shell completions.

## Published 0.33.1

[ShadowCode 0.33.1](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/releases/tag/v0.33.1) was published on September 28, 2026 from `e15c4480e65db5650af012bb2a9773dbe89acf84`. It improves editing, explicit verification, provider sign-in recovery and long-running desktop reliability. Historical notes below retain their original versions and scope.

## Everyday workflow

- **Editor.** Code highlighting, line numbers, undo/redo and recoverable drafts. Saves check the original disk revision, preserve supported newline formats and retain edits typed while a save is pending.
- **Context.** Inspect the files and bounded excerpts attached to the next task, including exclusions, truncation and approximate token counts. Estimates are not provider-reported usage.
- **Run a check…** Completed-task summaries can start a fresh, user-entered command against current project files without selecting a model or spending another model turn. Existing trust and command approvals apply. Output and a new receipt appear in a new task while your composer draft and earlier evidence remain intact. A successful command proves that check's result, not overall application correctness.
- **Accounts.** Returning to Settings restores each provider's active login independently. Cancellation shows **Stopping…** until acknowledged. Unknown progress preserves cached information instead of silently starting fresh probes. A successful login process alone does not establish Ready or subscription billing.

## Workspace and desktop reliability

- Compare refuses app-owned unsaved editor drafts before taking its snapshot. Short writes coordinate across cooperating ShadowCode processes, and interrupted cleanup retains ownership evidence and recoverable work. Arbitrary terminal commands and external applications remain outside that cooperative lock.
- Shared native event registrations avoid growth on every task. A source-built X11 run passed 100 qualification tasks after 25 warm-up tasks with stable listener, descriptor and thread counts and intact SQLite integrity.
- AppImage launch preserves an explicit display-backend choice. The package normalizer accepts linuxdeploy's single exact matching version field while rejecting unrelated launcher changes.
- Approval restoration, provider event ownership, cancellation, local-model scheduling and installer recovery have additional regression coverage.

## Release and qualification status

The runtime builder now preserves tracked source pins and reference metadata during ordinary builds and notices-only refreshes. Generated runtime metadata retains the actual compilation time. Shell-flow regressions cover the two input mutations that stopped the unpublished 0.33.0 release; the immutable-source guard remains enforced.

Release jobs separate build, signing and publication, verify private artifact snapshots and require complete scoped receipts. The AppImage installer requires publisher signatures and durable accepted-state checks; checksum overrides and `--unverified` do not bypass authentication. Previously published unsigned artifacts are not retroactively authenticated.

Recorded source evidence includes 507 UI unit tests, 75 browser scenarios and the 100-task native endurance run. These counts describe the tested source snapshots, not automatically the final 0.33.1 package. Small live coding tasks have passed across Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok and Antigravity; full live login-expiry/cancellation/continuation qualification and ACP billing entitlement remain separate.

[Checks 36418625715](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/actions/runs/36418625715) and [Native desktop 36418625663](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/actions/runs/36418625663) passed on the release commit. [Release run 36427024374](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/actions/runs/36427024374), attempt 1, passed all 15 required build gates and protected signing. Its publication job failed when the new draft was briefly absent from the release listing, so the workflow retains a failure conclusion. Publication resumed locally using the same frozen publisher at `e15c448` and immutable signed artifact `10987931982`; all seven remote asset files were downloaded and compared before the release became public. The tag and package bytes were preserved. A fresh download of all seven public assets matched the signed artifact byte for byte, and offline verification of the public AppImage passed against the independently reviewed trust bundle, expected version and full commit.

Physical COSMIC/Wayland interaction coverage is partial: the overall run failed its requested window-resize assertions. GPU inference endurance and broader keyboard/clipboard/IME/DPI acceptance are not established. See the [implementation evidence ledger](FLAGSHIP_IMPLEMENTATION.md) for exact snapshots, retained failures and later results.

The [published Linux release](https://github.com/ShadowfetchStudio/ShadowCode/releases/tag/v0.33.1) includes `ShadowCode_0.33.1_amd64.AppImage`, `ShadowCode_0.33.1_amd64.deb` and `ShadowCode_0.33.1_appimage-runtime-sources.tar.gz`, together with `SHA256SUMS`, `RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`, `RELEASE-AUTH` and `RELEASE-AUTH.sig`. Use the [release procedure](RELEASING.md) and [publisher authentication contract](RELEASE_AUTHENTICATION.md) to verify packages with independently trusted installer tooling.

## Published 0.32.0

ShadowCode 0.32.0 is the biggest update yet: it's easier to use every day,
the agent is smarter, commands are properly sandboxed, and you can use
ShadowCode from your phone, your editor, or on a schedule. The 0.31.1 notes
follow below.

## Easier every day

- **Type `@` to attach files** and folders, **↑** for earlier prompts, and
  switch between **Code, Plan and Ask** right in the composer. Models that
  support it get an **effort** control.
- **Edit and resend** any of your messages, or retry or copy it.
- **Approvals show the actual change:** the diff for a file, the full
  command for a shell step. **Allow for this task** stops repeat prompts,
  and **Deny with note** tells the agent why.
- **Review just what a task changed**, full width, and keep or undo each
  change. **Rewind** now asks first, can be undone, and also covers shell
  commands and Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok and Antigravity edits.
- **Run tasks side by side:** **Worktree** next to Send starts a task in its
  own copy of the project; apply it, keep it as a branch or discard it.
- **Notifications** when a task needs you, fails, hits a plan limit or
  finishes; click to jump to it. The sidebar marks what needs attention.
- **See context and cost** for every model in the status bar.
- **Preview the app you're building** inside ShadowCode and click an
  element to show the agent exactly what to change.
- **A real terminal**, a **Git tab** that goes from commit to pull request
  with live CI checks, and **voice dictation** that runs on your computer.

## A smarter agent

- **Subagents** explore, plan, review or work in parallel copies of your
  project.
- **Language servers** tell the agent about errors right after each edit,
  and a **repo map** and **code search** help it find its way.
- Long conversations are **summarized** instead of cut, OpenRouter
  requests use **prompt caching**, and dropped connections are **retried**.
- It reads **CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules and Claude Code skills and commands**,
  and your MCP servers reach every model.

## Safer by default

- Shell commands run in a **sandbox that hides your home folder**: SSH
  keys, cloud credentials and API keys stay invisible, and only the project
  is writable. You can require the sandbox and limit the network to a list
  of hosts.

## Beyond the window

- **Remote access:** scan a QR code to follow and steer ShadowCode from your
  phone. Off by default; Tailscale recommended.
- **Zed and JetBrains:** `shadowcode acp` makes ShadowCode an agent inside
  your editor.
- **Automations:** run a prompt on a schedule, turn a GitHub issue into a
  task and pull request, or run ShadowCode in GitHub Actions.

## New in 0.31.0

- **Allowance.** One button in the status bar shows what's left everywhere:
  each subscription's usage and reset times, your OpenRouter credits, and the
  local models ready to run. Only figures the services report; nothing is
  guessed.
- **Keep going when a plan runs out.** When Codex, Claude Code or another
  subscription hits its limit, the same conversation continues on a local
  model, with a note saying so. Prefer to choose? Set **When a plan runs out**
  to **Ask me**. ShadowCode never retries on the same plan or buys more
  usage.
- **Compare.** Press **Compare** next to Send to give one task to 2 or 3
  models. Each works in its own copy of your project (uncommitted work
  included); see their changes, checks, time and cost side by side, then
  **Keep** the best one. Only the kept changes reach your files, nothing is
  committed, and the copies are cleaned up. **Wins in this project** tracks
  which model you keep. Tested live: two OpenRouter models fixed the same bug
  in 11 seconds and the kept fix applied cleanly.

## New in 0.30.0

- **Antigravity asks first.** It now runs through Google's official ACP agent
  server instead of the `agy` CLI's print mode, which silently denied any

  conversations resume.
- **One-time install.** **Settings › Accounts › Antigravity › Install**
  downloads the server from Google (334 MB, checksum-verified). **Connect**
  then signs in with Google in your browser. This sign-in is ShadowCode's own
  and separate from the `agy` CLI.
- **No surprise browser tabs.** Status checks and tasks never open a sign-in
  page. If the sign-in expires, the row says *Sign in* and a task stops with
  that message.

## ShadowCode 0.28.0

ShadowCode 0.28.0 is a Linux desktop coding agent with one window and one
model picker. It runs your existing subscriptions through the vendors' official
command-line tools, or GGUF models on your own hardware with a llama.cpp
runtime that ships with the app.

## What changed

- **One picker** lists **Subscriptions** and **On this computer**. Every row
  shows Local or Cloud, whether it is ready (and why not), Vision and Chat only
  badges, and the usage the vendor reports. Each conversation remembers its
  model.
- **Accounts.** **Settings › Accounts** signs in and out with each vendor's
  official login and logout commands. ShadowCode never reads credential files,
  and it removes provider API keys from the environment of every vendor task,
  login and logout.
- **Usage.** Codex shows its rate-limit windows per quota pool, with reset
  times. Other vendors show *Usage unavailable* with the reason. The last
  snapshot survives a restart. When a vendor reports its plan limit, the task
  stops and you pick another model.
- **Local models.** A pinned llama.cpp (Vulkan and every x86-64 CPU level) is
  bundled in the AppImage and the deb. Models are read from their GGUF
  metadata. Context is sized to your VRAM or RAM. Models in an existing Ollama
  store can be imported by reference, without copying and without the daemon.
  Vision comes from a paired projector.
- **Web tools for local models.** `web_fetch` and `web_search` block private
  networks and cloud metadata addresses.
- **Network modes.** Online, Web tools off, Offline.
- **Permission modes.** *Ask before actions* (the default for new installs) and
  *Allow project edits*. Settings explains what each vendor enforces.
- **Switching providers mid-conversation.** A bounded summary of the earlier
  turns is handed over, and ShadowCode asks your consent before local content
  goes to a cloud provider.
- **Resuming vendor sessions.** Each vendor's own session is resumed per
  conversation.
- **Installer.** `scripts/install-appimage.sh` now requires `SHA256SUMS` and
  installs the llama.cpp runtime from the AppImage into
  `~/.local/lib/shadowcode`, rolling back if a step fails.
- **Removed.** The legacy Python harness and its tooling.

## Subscription status

| Vendor | Runtime | Image input | Approvals shown in ShadowCode | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | `codex app-server` | Yes | Yes | Rate-limit windows per pool |
| Claude Code | `claude -p` stream-json | Yes | Yes | Unavailable |
| Cursor | `cursor-agent acp` | When advertised | Yes | Unavailable (plan tier only) |
| Antigravity | `agy --print=` stream-json | No | No (its own settings) | Unavailable |
| Grok | `grok agent stdio` (ACP) | No | Yes | Unavailable (session tokens only) |

## Local model support

- **Formats.** Any GGUF whose architecture the bundled llama.cpp supports.
  Unsupported ones (for example `gptoss` at this pin) are listed with the
  reason.
- **Hardware.** Vulkan GPUs, or any x86-64 CPU. One model is loaded at a time.
  If the GPU start fails, ShadowCode retries on the CPU and labels the row.
- **Tools and vision.** Models whose chat template has no tool support run as
  *Chat only*. Models with a paired projector accept images and get
  `view_image`.

## Known limits

- **Claude Code** was not verified end to end on the build machine, because it
  was not signed in there. The stream-json adapter is covered by unit
  tests with scripted protocol frames, and sign-in state by fake-CLI tests.
- **Antigravity** exposes no machine-readable usage. It never sends approval
  requests to ShadowCode: its own settings decide what it may do. Sign-in and
  sign-out happen only inside `agy`.
- **Cursor** reports its plan tier but no remaining allowance.
- **Grok**'s ACP interface accepts no images, and Grok has no read-only mode
  for Plan/Review.
- **`web_search`** uses DuckDuckGo's HTML page, which may block automated
  requests. The tool then reports that no results were retrieved.
- **Ollama stores outside `~/.ollama/models`** are found only through
  `OLLAMA_MODELS` or an `Environment=OLLAMA_MODELS` line in the Ollama systemd
  user unit. The system-wide service's store isn't found automatically.
- **ShadowCode is not an operating-system sandbox.** Shell commands run as
  your user.
